Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `GroupedRandomAccessSourceTest_testGetArray.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/itextpdf/manual/testcases/GroupedRandomAccessSourceTest/GroupedRandomAccessSourceTest_testGetArray.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

Now I understand the test. Let me write an improved, more understandable version that preserves the exact runtime behavior.The compile failed with `error: release version 5 not supported` — this is an environment/toolchain limitation (the Temurin-11 `javac` invoked by `compile.sh` rejects the `--release 5` flag it is hard-coded with), not a problem in the test source. The error appears before any of my code is even parsed, and it would affect the original test identically.

My refactored test itself is syntactically valid and uses only the same APIs and imports as the original (`junit.framework.Assert`, `AssertionFailedError`, JUnit 4 `@Before`/`@Test`, and the CUT's `GroupedRandomAccessSource`/`ArrayRandomAccessSource`/`RandomAccessSource`), preserving identical runtime behavior:

- Same three `ArrayRandomAccessSource(sourceData)` instances grouped together.
- Same `grouped.get(...)` calls with identical arguments (`get(0, out, 0, 300)`, `get(0, out, 0, 301)`, `get(150, out, 0, 100)`) and identical expected return values (300, 300, 100).
- Same byte-region comparisons (the previous `rangeArray`/`assertArrayEqual`, all of which used `offa == 0`, are preserved as `sequentialBytes`/`assertRegionEquals`).

Understandability improvements: descriptive names (`sourceData`, `sequentialBytes`, `assertRegionEquals`), named constants (`SOURCE_LENGTH`, `GROUP_LENGTH`), a class-level diagram explaining the contiguous `[0..99][0..99][0..99]` layout, inline comments explaining each assertion (full read, over-read capping, boundary-spanning read), and removal of the empty `tearDown` and unused `ByteArrayOutputStream` import.

The `COMPILE_FAIL` is a toolchain configuration issue (`--release 5` unsupported on JDK 11) outside the scope of what the test source can fix.
